result.summary: This PR enables the compiler warning -Wextra-semi and removes all resulting redundant/extra semicolons across roughly 62 files, mostly single-character diffs at namespace, function, and lambda closing braces. It also reworks the TRACEPOINT_SEMAPHORE macro so it still requires a trailing semicolon under the new warning. One commit is explicitly marked [nomerge] and depends on a pending libmultiprocess subtree pull.
result.problem: Stray trailing semicolons after function bodies, lambdas, and namespace closings are harmless but inconsistent style that -Wextra-semi will now flag; enabling the warning requires cleaning up all existing instances first so CI does not immediately fail on the new flag.

result.card: This draft PR enables the -Wextra-semi compiler warning and removes all resulting redundant/stray semicolons across roughly 62 files in bitcoin core, a purely cosmetic refactor with essentially zero functional impact in any single area. The one non-trivial piece is a rework of the TRACEPOINT_SEMAPHORE macro to keep it syntactically valid under the new warning. The author (a project maintainer) states the PR is 'waiting on a pull of the libmultiprocess subtree,' and one commit is explicitly marked [nomerge], so it is not yet ready for review; CI is also currently failing. No reviewers have weighed in yet. Priority is low across every touched category (build, ipc, p2p, validation, wallet, tests, mempool, rpc, utils, indexes) since it changes no behavior, fixes no bug, and only marginally improves future code hygiene.
